identity.real_world_identity_notes: The exact simulator identity maps to the Alpine A110 Cup introduced for the Alpine Europa Cup in 2018. Alpine's own material identifies a 3MO six-speed sequential transmission operated by steering-wheel controls and an integrated steering-wheel display. The reviewed sources do not establish the internal engagement construction, physical clutch operation, exact shift-cut/blip strategy, or rim topology beyond the display/control functions.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: The reviewed exact-scope sources establish forward gears: 6; shift actuation: sequential paddles; shift pattern: sequential; transmission upshift manual_blip: not applicable; transmission upshift automatic_blip: not applicable; transmission downshift throttle_lift: not applicable; transmission downshift automatic_cut: not applicable; integrated wheel display: yes.
The reviewed real-car sources do not establish launch technique, running-shift technique, cut and blip behavior or wheel topology; those baseline fields remain unknown.

Alpine's official competition page and technical material identify the A110 Cup, the 3MO six-speed sequential gearbox, and the steering-wheel controls/display. The 2018 launch material identifies the Europa Cup introduction. No existing curated record matches the exact identity.

claims.basis: Alpine's official competition page and technical material identify the A110 Cup, the 3MO six-speed sequential gearbox, and the steering-wheel controls/display. The 2018 launch material identifies the Europa Cup introduction. No existing curated record matches the exact identity.

All official technical sources specify six sequential ratios. The official material explicitly places paddle-shift controls on the steering wheel. The gearbox is explicitly described as sequential. The reviewed sources describe paddle sequential operation and no upshift rev-match action; blip is not an upshift field for this evidence. The reviewed sources do not describe an upshift automatic blip action. No separate downshift throttle-lift procedure is stated; the relevant unresolved field is rev matching or automatic control. The sources do not describe a downshift torque-cut action. Alpine explicitly specifies an integrated display in the steering wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/gearbox_type, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.
